answer:
Given matrix:
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

1. **Apply elementary row operations to reduce to row echelon / row-reduced echelon form:**
   Perform $R_2 \to R_2 + R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - R_1$:
   $$\sim \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$|

   Multiply $R_1$ by $-1$:
   $$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$|

   Perform $R_3 \to 4R_3 + 3R_2$:
   $$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$|

   To get row-reduced echelon form, scale rows to make leading entries 1 and clear columns:
   $$R_3 \to \frac{1}{5}R_3 \implies \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$|
   $$R_2 \to \frac{1}{4}R_2 \implies \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1/4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$|
   Eliminate above pivots:
   $$R_1 \to R_1 - 2R_3, \quad R_2 \to R_2 + \frac{1}{4}R_3$$
   $$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$|
   $$R_1 \to R_1 + 2R_2$$
   $$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$|

2. **Find the Rank:**
   Since there are 3 non-zero rows in the echelon form, $\text{rank}(A) = 3$.
proTip: The rank of a matrix equals the number of non-zero rows in its row echelon form.
